issues.description: Docs ship example code that was never executed — `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is gratuitous when `pipeline.nodes[0]` works
issues.detail: The Basic usage block uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to grab the first node. This is cleverness where obvious wins: `pipeline.nodes[0]` is shorter, faster, and what any maintainer would write. Worse, none of these snippets appear to have been run — there's no indication anyone copy-pasted them into a REPL to confirm `preview.to_dict()` exists and returns what the comment claims. Docs that haven't been executed rot. Run every snippet, then ship them.

issues.description: Three patches submitted as one — docs change is mixed with two unrelated style-config edits
issues.detail: This diff touches `.github/styles/Kedro/headings.yml` (add JSON exception), `.github/styles/Kedro/ignore.txt` (add lowercase polars), and `docs/build/nodes.md` (the actual feature docs). These are three logically independent changes. The Vale config tweaks are byproducts of getting the docs to lint; they should be their own commit at minimum so a future bisect or revert of the docs change doesn't drag along orthogonal style-config edits. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Adding lowercase `polars` to ignore.txt when `Polars` is already there is papering over a real spelling issue
issues.detail: `Polars` already exists in ignore.txt as the proper-noun form. Adding lowercase `polars` means the prose somewhere writes the brand name lowercased. Either the prose should be fixed (it's a proper noun) or this is a deliberate exception that needs a comment explaining why. Quietly duplicating the entry in two cases is the kind of style-config drift that compounds over years.

issues.description: Author's own checklist admits no tests and no RELEASE.md entry; docs describe behavior that may not be locked down
issues.detail: The PR checklist shows `Added tests to cover my changes` and `Added a description of this change in RELEASE.md` unchecked. This is a docs-only PR for an experimental feature, fine — but the docs assert concrete API contracts (`preview_fn` kwarg on `node()`, `node.preview()` method, `to_dict()` on every preview type, `meta` keys like `language` and the Mermaid config schema) that aren't covered by tests in this diff. If the underlying #5317 changes shape, these docs lie. At minimum, link the docs to a doctested example or note explicitly which kedro-viz version honors `meta.language` and the Mermaid config keys.

issues.description: Dead code in example — unreachable return after first `return` in ImagePreview snippet
issues.detail: In the Image preview block, the function has `return ImagePreview(content="https://...")` followed by a commented-out alternative. The structure pretends the second form is an alternative but a reader copy-pasting hits the URL form and never sees the data-URI variant unless they read the comment. Either show two separate functions (Option 1 / Option 2 style, like the Table preview section already does) or use a clear `# Or, alternatively:` block above a single example. Consistency with the Table preview section's own pattern would help.

issues.description: Mermaid config example claims defaults (`default: 250`, `default: 50`) without citing source — these will drift
issues.detail: The custom_config block annotates each key with a default value in a comment. Defaults belong to upstream Mermaid, not Kedro. The moment Mermaid changes a default, this doc is wrong and nobody will notice. Either drop the `(default: X)` annotations and link to the schema (which is already linked below), or generate them from the upstream source. Hand-maintained mirrors of upstream defaults are a maintenance trap.

issues.description: `node(...)` snippets at module top level are not runnable as shown
issues.detail: Several code blocks show `node(func=..., inputs=..., outputs=..., preview_fn=..., name=...)` as a bare call with no surrounding pipeline, no assignment, and no import in some cases. A reader copy-pasting hits NameError or just a dangling expression. Either wrap each in a `Pipeline([...])` like the first example, or annotate clearly that these are fragments. Docs that don't run as written waste reader time.

issues.description: `make_preview_fn` closure example demonstrates closure mechanics but the prose says preview functions can `access datasets within the preview function` with no example of how
issues.detail: The section promises two patterns — closures and dataset access — and only delivers the closure pattern. If accessing datasets from a preview_fn is supported and recommended, show it (with the catalog handle, lifecycle warnings, the works). If it's not really supported, drop the claim. Half-promises in docs become support tickets.

review.summary: Docs-only PR for an experimental `preview_fn` feature. The writing is clear and the example coverage across preview types is genuinely useful. But the diff is three patches in a trenchcoat (Vale headings, Vale ignore, the actual docs), at least one code example uses gratuitous cleverness (`next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)`) where indexing is obvious, several snippets aren't runnable as written, and the Mermaid config example hand-mirrors upstream defaults that will drift. Author's own checklist admits no tests for the feature these docs describe — so if #5317 reshapes the API, these docs silently lie. NEEDS-WORK: split the Vale changes out, run every snippet through a REPL before shipping, drop the upstream-default annotations, and either deliver or remove the dataset-access claim.
